thread:
claire: Heads-up, saw 3 CUDA OOMs in prod (inference-1, eu-west) right after the 08:02 deploy. Rolled back the release to restore capacity. Log snippet below.

claire: ```
[2026-03-18T08:09:11Z] model=instruct-34b instance=inf-1 seq_len=8192 alloc_kv=1342177280 cuda_error=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
stack: runtime::alloc_kv -> attention_kv::reserve -> cudaMalloc -> OOM
```

dan: Which PR/commit went out in that deploy? Any quick bisect pointers?

claire: Deploy was tag `release-2026-03-18` -> includes merges up to `abc1234`. The suspect change in the release notes is the kernel-selection heuristic + batching tweak: `prefer_fused_for_shortseqs` and `batch_delay_ms=5` (was 2).

ben: Reproduced locally on a dev node with long-context load (seqlen ~8k) and batch size 1. I profiled memory allocation - looks like fragmentation + lots of cudaMallocs for KV slices. Perf snippet:```
free_before=5.1GB free_after=1.2GB # after a few requests
malloc_count+=124 per-request
avg_alloc_size=10.4MB
peak_rss_device=11.7GB
```
This smells like the kernel change caused codepaths to allocate temporary KV-backed buffers instead of reusing the pre-reserved pool.

emma: I bisected to the merge `abc1234` (merge PR #4829). The PR switched kernel selection to favor the fused-attn kernel for short per-head sequences, but the fused implementation uses an internal staging buffer when seq_len > threshold which triggers extra device allocs. Steps to reproduce:
```
# quick repro (docker + small model shim)
./run_infer --model instruct-34b --seq 8192 --batch 1 --repeat 50
watch -n 0.5 nvidia-smi -l 0.5
# observe repeated cudaMalloc/free + fragmentation growth
```

dan: Good find. CI didn't catch this because our perf tests use seq_len=2048 and batching patterns that mask the alloc pattern. The change interacts badly with long-seq, batch=1 traffic.

ben: Also noticed the KV cache eviction path: we recently changed the eviction to return freed KV slices to the allocator immediately (vs keeping a small pool). Now with the fused kernel allocating more small chunks, the global allocator is doing many more small frees/allocs -> fragmentation.

claire: TL;DR: fused kernel + changed eviction strategy + slightly higher batch delay = fragmentation -> OOM on longctx runs.

sre-oncall: Assigning this to eng-runtime urgent. Proposed short-term mitigations: revert kernel-selection change or force preallocation of a reserved KV slab per model instance, and reduce batch_delay back to 2ms.

ben: I can open a hotfix PR to: (1) revert the kernel preference (fastest path), (2) reintroduce a small KV freelist reserve, and (3) add a CI perf job targeting seq_len=8192, batch=1 to catch regressions.

emma: I'll add a regression test to the eval harness and a micro-benchmark for fused kernel path that measures malloc_count and fragmentation metrics.

infra-bot: deploybot: rollback of `release-2026-03-18` initiated by claire at 08:18 UTC. Instances being replaced: inference-1, inference-2. :arrow_backward:

claire: After rollback memory pressure dropped immediately on the affected hosts. No new OOMs since 08:22.

dan: Action items: ben to open hotfix PR (target: revert kernel-selection + freelist reserve), emma to add CI perf test, sre-oncall to monitor prod for 24h. I'll own rollout of the hotfix once approved.

ben: PR draft up at https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4891 - includes benchmark results comparing fragmentation before/after.

emma: pinging infra to schedule a non-prod stress run with mixed batch sizes and seq up to 16k so we can validate.

sre-oncall: Monitoring: added alert rule to trigger if device free drops >2GB within 60s on any host.

claire: Thanks all. We'll keep this thread updated with the hotfix CI run + canary rollout notes. :thumbsup:
